Faculty research spans pure mathematics, statistics, mathematics education, computational science, and consulting-fueling programs accredited by CAC/ABET. Undergraduates can pursue a B.S. degree in Mathematics with options in Applied Mathematics/Statistics or Pure Mathematics with Secondary Teacher Preparation. Graduate students choose from two separate degrees-MS in Mathematics or MS in Statistics and Applied Mathematics-with flexible thesis or exam culminating experience. The department emphasizes practical problem-solving skills, supporting interdisciplinary education and quantitative analysis for careers in industry, government, education, and research. Students connect with real-world data and statistics through the Consulting Center for Statistics & Applied Mathematics (CCSAM), regional outreach via California Mathematics Project, and collaborative research in the NSF-funded REU. Honors society chapter Kappa Mu Epsilon recognizes academic excellence. Outreach initiatives include “Gift of Numbers,” where students introduce math through games at local schools. The department also provides scholarships, teaching associate roles, and regular colloquia, ensuring strong professional and community connections. This enriching ecosystem empowers students with both advanced analytical training and real-world experience essential for success across diverse careers. Programs Bachelor Mathematics

courses.title: Special Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at graduate level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Problem Solving as a Mathematical Endeavor
courses.description: Heuristics and strategies to solve mathematical problems, impact of technology in solving problems and in teaching problem solving, reformulation of problems and problem posing techniques, presentation of outcomes. Introduction to the mathematical problem solving literature.

courses.title: Research in Mathematics Education
courses.description: This course is a graduate seminar on research in mathematics education. The aim is an introduction to research in the field of mathematics education with an emphasis on the roles of educational theory, qualitative and quantitative research paradigms and methodologies, the analysis and critique of research.

courses.title: Research Methods in Mathematics Education
courses.description: Graduate course on research methods in mathematics education. Introduction to the various research methods used in the field of mathematics education, with a focus on the roles of educational theory, qualitative and quantitative research paradigms and methodologies. Development of research questions and study design.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions, logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: College Algebra Activity
courses.description: An activity course to support and provide practice and hands-on activities for MAT 1050 College Algebra. Corequisite(s): MAT 1050 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: College Algebra Stretch I
courses.description: This is the first of a two-course stretch sequence in College Algebra. The theory and application of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformation, and equations. Emphasis on polynomial, rational, radical and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions. Required for students in GE Math Category IV in STEM fields, recommended for students in GE Math Category III. Corequisite(s): MAT 1051A .

courses.title: College Algebra Stretch I Activity
courses.description: An activity course to support and provide practice and hands-on activities for MAT 1051, College Algebra Stretch I. Corequisite(s): MAT 1051 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: College Algebra Stretch II
courses.description: [GE 2] This is the second of a two course sequence in College Algebra. The theory and applications of real-valued functions. Graphing and solving equations with exponential and logarithmic functions. Equations and inequalities, including polynomial and absolutely value inequalities. Systems of equations, both linear and nonlinear. Symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.

courses.title: College Algebra with Support
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions,inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions,logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions. Corequisite(s): MAT 1055A .

courses.title: College Algebra with Support Activity
courses.description: An activity course to support and provide practice and hands-on activities for MAT1050 College Algebra. Corequisite(s): MAT 1055 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Trigonometry
courses.description: [GE 2] Right triangle trigonometry, the unit circle, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions, trigonometric identities, equations, graphs, Law of Sines and Law of Cosines, applications of trigonometry, complex numbers and DeMoivre’s Formula. Applications of trigonometry to solve problems.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Precalculus
courses.description: [GE 2] Basic concepts of trigonometry and algebra including the theory of real-valued functions, the unit circle, equations and inequalities, absolute value, and graphing. Emphasis on power functions, polynomials, rational functions, exponential functions, trigonometric functions, piecewise functions, and their inverses. Applications of trigonometry and algebra.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS>=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Functions, limits, continuity, derivatives of all functions including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic, inverse trigonometric, and implicit functions. Applications of derivatives, including max/min problems and L’Hopitals rule. Definite and Indefinite Integrals, The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, substitution rule and applications.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Supplemental Instruction for Calculus Activity
courses.description: Provides supplemental instruction for students concurrently enrolled in MAT 1140. Corequisite(s): MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Calculus Bridge for Transcendental Functions
courses.description: Derivatives and integrals of transcendental functions. Includes exponential functions, logarithms, trigonometric and inverse trigonometric functions. Review of concepts of first semester calculus, including differentiation, related rates, optimization, the fundamental theorem of calculus, integration, and area between curves. This course is for students who have taken a first semester calculus course for engineering and science majors that does not transfer as MAT 1140 due to not fully covering transcendental functions. Students should confer with department to determine whether they qualify for this course.

courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: [GE 2] Integration techniques including integration by parts, integrals of trigonometric products, partial fractions, substitution and trigonometric substitution. Hyperbolic functions. Improper Integrals, sequences and series, polar coordinates, parametric equations and conic sections.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB >=3, AP Calc BC >=3, or C or better in MAT 1140 or MAT 1140C.

courses.title: Calculus for Life Sciences
courses.description: [GE 2] Concepts of functions and the idea of change. Review of algebraic, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions. Brief review of fundamental topics in right triangle trigonometry. Graphing, limits, derivatives, differentials, and integrals of single variable functions listed above. Optimization problems and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Special emphasis is given to applications in life sciences.
courses.prerequisites: AP PreCalculus >=3, ALEKS Comp >=61, C or better in MAT 1050 , C or better in MAT 1052 , C or better in MAT 1055 , or C or better in MAT 1070 .

courses.title: Introductory Calculus for Business
courses.description: [GE 2] Graphing and functions including exponentials and logarithms, derivatives and basic differentiation rules, curve sketching, anti-derivatives, integration, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. A special emphasis is placed on business applications such as break-even analysis, supply and demand, optimization, average cost, marginal analysis, and consumer-producer surplus.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Technical Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Differential and integral calculus of polynomial, rational, trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions, with applications of the derivative and the integral.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Technical Calculus II
courses.description: Infinite series, an introduction to ordinary differential equations and Laplace transforms.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1300B.

courses.title: Quantitative Reasoning and Problem-Solving
courses.description: This course aims to develop problem solving skills and critical thinking through varied problem situations. Each situation will allow the exploration of mathematical content, including: decimals, percents, fractions, multiplicative reasoning, algebraic symbolism, functions and their representations, sequences and statistical measures. This course is designed for students who intend to enroll in MAT 1940. Required for students in Category IV. Corequisite(s): MAT 1900A .

courses.title: Quantitative Reasoning and Problem-Solving Activity
courses.description: An activity course to support and provide practice and hands-on activities for MAT 1900. Corequisite(s): MAT 1900 .

courses.title: Survey of Mathematics
courses.description: [GE 2] Modern applications of mathematics. Selected topics from: voting and social choice, fairness and game theory, money management, cryptography, symmetry and patterns, applications to art and music, logic and puzzles, etc. Corequisite(s): MAT 1910A (only if Category III or IV).
courses.prerequisites: Category I, II, III, or IV.

courses.title: Survey of Mathematics Activity
courses.description: An activity course to support, and provide practice and hands-on activities for MAT 1910 Survey of Mathematics. Corequisite(s): MAT 1910 .
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 1 unit per semester.

courses.title: Mathematical Concepts for Elementary School Teachers
courses.description: [GE 2] Deep analysis of the Number and Quantity Domain of the Common Core Standards in Mathematics for K-8 students. Deep understanding of numbers systems, the operations among them, their meaning and different algorithms that can be used. Identification of the conceptual foundation for these algorithms. Modeling of the Standards of Mathematical Practice. Emphasis on the use of different representations and different models for mathematical ideas. Discussion of the role of precise language and notation in the development of mathematical thinking. Analysis of different ways of argumentation in mathematics. This course has a field work component. This course has a field work component.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1900 or MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Introduction to Computational Methods in Mathematics
courses.description: An introduction to problem solving using computational tools. Problems will be drawn from a variety of modern topics in mathematics including calculus, algebra, combinatorics, number theory, probability, and statistics. Includes discussion on how numbers are represented on a computer and the numerical error introduced. Corequisite(s): MAT 2010L .
